source.title: The serotonin-1A receptor in anxiety disorders

confidence_rationale: High-quality, well-cited review synthesising 5-HT1A KO/transgenic mouse models, human genetic polymorphisms, and PET binding (WAY-100635) data, all converging on a key role for 5-HT1A in the serotonergic regulation of anxiety, with reduced 5-HT1A binding in panic and social anxiety disorder. Grounds the layer's assignment of the aversive/anxiety (terrain) arm to 5-HT1A. Confidence mid-range because (a) it is a review not a single decisive experiment, (b) the data implicate limbic/temporal and raphe 5-HT1A broadly rather than isolating a hippocampal-CA1/DG basin-depth mechanism, and (c) 'aversive attractor basin depth' is REE's construct, not measured here.
failure_signatures: The review localises the anxiety-relevant 5-HT1A signal to limbic/mesiotemporal cortex and raphe autoreceptors broadly and notably finds 5-HT1A binding NOT reduced in PTSD -- so the layer's specific 'MECH-088 PTSD terrain component' attribution to 5-HT1A is weakened, not supported, by the human PET pattern.
Pre-synaptic (raphe autoreceptor) vs post-synaptic 5-HT1A have opposite functional signs, so a single '5-HT1A = terrain' assignment conflates two populations.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Convergent preclinical (5-HT1A knockout/transgenic mice), genetic (human polymorphisms associated with higher anxiety), and neuroimaging (PET) evidence implicates the inhibitory 5-HT1A receptor in the neural processing of anxiety; PET shows reduced 5-HT1A binding in panic disorder and social anxiety disorder (but not PTSD), and higher trait anxiety associates with lower 5-HT1A binding in healthy subjects.
mapping.ree_translation: The receptor layer assigns MECH-085's hippocampal-terrain motif -- aversive attractor basin depth / fear-consistent rollout capture -- to 5-HT1A (median-raphe-driven, hippocampal CA1/DG + somatodendritic autoreceptor), distinct from the 5-HT2A cortical/narrative arm. Akimova et al. ground the functional half of that assignment: 5-HT1A tone is causally and clinically tied to anxiety/aversive state, and 5-HT1A partial agonism (buspirone, PHARM-016) is the predicted terrain-flattening lever.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review supports '5-HT1A modulates aversive/anxiety state', not the specific REE construct 'hippocampal-CA1/DG aversive-basin depth'. The human binding signal localises to mesiotemporal cortex and raphe broadly, and is explicitly NOT reduced in PTSD -- which sits awkwardly with the layer's PTSD-terrain attribution. Pre- vs post-synaptic 5-HT1A populations have opposite signs and are not separated in this mapping.
mapping.source_context: Human (PET, genetics) + mouse (KO/transgenic); narrative review, anxiety disorders.

confidence_components.notes: Strong convergent review. Mapping_fidelity moderate: grounds 5-HT1A-anxiety link cleanly but not the CA1/DG basin-depth specificity, and the PTSD-null finding is a partial counter to one sub-attribution. Transfer risk low-moderate (substantial human data).
